title: Cap. IV Arg. 4 Sol: Major — temporal election of actual believers vs eternal gift of faith in Christ
pass_a_gloss: But the ventilation of the conclusion having been dismissed I come to the Major; which was of this sort, The election by which God chose us in Christ is only of believers. If this proposition be understood of temporal election, by which certain persons are severed from the world of the wicked through efficacious vocation, we acknowledge that this election is only of believers, and of actually believing ones: but we dispute concerning the eternal act of the Divine election, not concerning the temporal effect of the same. If therefore they regard this eternal election, which in this controversy they ought to regard, we say that this election is not of believers, as if certain men still constituted outside Christ were foreseen by God as believers, and with this foreseen faith intervening were elected; but is of believers, because God foresaw that he would give the gift of faith to those whom in the eternal purpose of election he decreed to give to Christ.
pass_b_english: Drop the conclusion and take the Major: The election by which God chose us in Christ is of believers only. If that means temporal election — certain persons severed from the wicked world by efficacious vocation — we grant it is of believers, and of actually believing ones. But we dispute the eternal act of divine election, not its temporal effect. So of eternal election (what this controversy must regard): it is not of believers as if men still outside Christ were foreseen as believers and then elected with that foresight intervening; it is of believers because God foresaw he would give the gift of faith to those he decreed in the eternal purpose of election to give to Christ.
source_text: Sed missa conclusionis ventilatione accedo ad Majorem; quae fuit hujusmodi, Electio qua nos Deus elegit in Christo est tantum credentium. Si de electione temporali, qua certae personae per vocationem efficacem a mundo improborum secernuntur, intelligatur haec propositio, agnoscimus hanc electionem esse tantum credentium, et actualiter credentium: sed nos de aeterno electionis Divinae actu, non de temporali ejusdem effectu, disputamus. Si ergo hanc aeternam electionem respiciant, quam in hac controversia respicere debent, dicimus hanc electionem non esse credentium, quasi quidam homines extra Christum adhuc constituti praeviderentur a Deo ut credentes, et interveniente hac fide praevisa eligerentur; sed esse credentium, quia Deus praevidit se illis donum fidei daturum, quos in aeterno electionis proposito Christo dare decrevit.
